question: Will the Bishkek City Court's appellate verdict in the 'Letter 75' case have been issued by September 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: As of 2026-09-07 the Bishkek City Court appellate proceeding is at its terminal stage: case materials examined that morning, closing arguments held that afternoon (prosecutors demanding 9 years each), only defendants' last words and deliberation remaining. Two separate defence attorneys have publicly forecast the ruling for 'next week' (24.kg, Sept 4) and specifically Sept 10 (AKIpress, Sept 7 17:11) — seven days before the Sept 17 deadline. Reference class of criminal proceedings that have reached closing arguments with a ~10-day deadline resolves YES roughly 80% of the time; the district-court phase of this same case went from arguments to pronounced verdict inside one day. Against that: this appeal has postponed ~3 of ~7 scheduled sittings (Aug 10->13, Aug 24->27, Aug 27->Sept 3), with gaps of 7-11 days, so a single adjournment after Sept 10 could consume the buffer; sessions are closed, and the case is politically charged (a real prison term for a former GKNB chief is a consequential call that could be held). September cadence of 2-3 sittings per week and the fact that a remand also counts as YES both push up. Modelling P(fail Sept 10) ~0.45 x P(fail again across the remaining week) ~0.35 gives ~0.84. No prediction market prices this event.

(5) Unsettled: Run 4 correctly flags that the criteria's main text lists 'remanded without a ruling' as NO while the fine print counts a remand as a qualifying disposition; no web access this run and the dossiers cannot resolve it, so I leave a small residual for that branch instead of treating remand as a closed failure path. Pure-judgment residue - how much weight the politically consequential choice between probation and nine years for a former GKNB chief gives to stalling - has no supporting evidence in any dossier (no recusal motion, illness, recess or holiday found), so I price it as a genuine but small tail rather than hedging toward the middle.
